question: How many UNESCO World Heritage Sites are present in India?(As of 2025)
solution:
The correct answer is __**44**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India has **44 UNESCO World Heritage Sites** as of 2025, making it one of the countries with a rich cultural and natural heritage.
 
• UNESCO World Heritage Sites are designated for their **unique cultural, historical, scientific, or other significance**.
 
• The sites include **35 cultural**, **8 natural**, and 1** mixed heritage sites** spread across the country.
 
• Notable examples include the Taj Mahal, Red Fort Complex, Kaziranga National Park, and the Western Ghats.
 
• India's heritage sites are recognized globally for their **contribution to human civilization and biodiversity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites**

 
 
• These sites are designated under the **1972 UNESCO World Heritage Convention**, which aims to protect and preserve cultural and natural heritage of international importance.
 
• The designation is based on stringent criteria such as **historical significance, uniqueness, and preservation standards**.
 
• Countries submit nominations to UNESCO, and the World Heritage Committee assesses and approves them.
 
 
 
• **India's Latest Additions**
 
 
• India's 43rd site is the **Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysala**, added in 2023.
 
• The Hoysala temples, located in Karnataka, are known for their intricate carvings and unique architectural style.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Heritage Sites**
 
 
• UNESCO World Heritage Sites contribute to **cultural tourism**, boosting local economies and creating awareness about preservation.
 
• They also serve as **educational resources**, helping people understand history, art, and biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **India's Representation**
 
 
• India ranks high globally in terms of the number of World Heritage Sites, showcasing its **diverse cultural and natural heritage**.
 
• The sites reflect India's **rich history, architectural ingenuity, and ecological diversity**.
